answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing new identities against the live tide of registrations: each applicant locks a deposit equal to the median stake times a factor that grows with how many unseasoned accounts appeared this epoch. An established miner must also sign a quill of sponsorship and share slash liability if that account later votes as a pack. Farms that keep minting personas then enter a spiral of superlinear bonds and longer seasoning delays, so cloning identities destroys expected profit.
